Own the clustered virtualization platform at production scale on the hypervisor of record: cluster design, shared storage presentation, converged networking, host lifecycle, and cluster-level troubleshooting. Engineer platform transitions, hypervisor version upgrades, host refresh, and any platform migration, as repeatable, controlled waves: capacity and rightsizing rules, conversion or upgrade, validation, cutover, and rollback. Coordinate execution with assigned engineers and project leads. Data Center Capacity and Facilities. Maintain a forward capacity model for compute, power, rack, cooling, and space across sites, using growth trends, utilization, support dates, and procurement lead times. Own facility requirements with colocation providers, including cage and rack layout, circuit and PDU allocation, cabling standards, physical access, and remote hands. Make assumptions and decision deadlines visible, and propose expansion ahead of the limit. Storage Architecture and Capacity. Design enterprise block (SAN) and scale-out file (NAS) architectures, including replication, thin provisioning, tiering, encryption at rest, and key-management dependencies. Model growth per platform against support dates and lead times; size expansions and deliver refresh designs ahead of end-of-life and capacity limits. Network Architecture and Capacity. Specify and validate network changes arising from infrastructure programs; day-to-day network engineering and device operations remain with network engineers and partners. Recovery and Continuity. Lead restore validation at scale and multi-site failover and failback against agreed recovery objectives. Reconcile continuity inventories against test results with application owners, and report unverified capabilities explicitly. L3 Escalation and Observability. Execute changes under peer review, risk assessment, and rollback requirements. Operational Readiness and Knowledge Transfer.
